scenario: AITA for visiting my son unannounced. | My son’s(19) in an university. He’s in a different city and lives in an apartment with 2 of his friends. Ever since he left(2 months ago) he just started ignoring me. I didn’t call him excessively, maybe once in two days. He’d hang up or not answer and text me later that he’s busy. Few days ago I was in the city for unrelated reason. I called him because I wanted to visit him but he didn’t answer so I just went to the apartment. His friend answered the door, my son was sleeping. The apartment was filthy, empty bottles everywhere, 5 or more ashtrays filled with cigarette butts. Dirty dishes to the roof. My son woke up and he was surprised when he saw me. He told me that I should’ve called him or something. We talked for a bit and he seemed kinda annoyed. I joked about the place needing a good clean and he just rolled his eyes. I asked him why he was ignoring me. He said that he’s just busy with studying and all that stuff and I should give him space when he needs it. He also said that it was weird that I just showed up unannounced.

prediction.raw: I would say 1, YTA (You're The Asshole). Here's why: Visiting your son unannounced, especially when he's made it clear that he needs space, can be seen as overstepping and disrespecting his boundaries. While it's understandable that you miss your son and want to see him, showing up at his apartment without warning can be perceived as intrusive and controlling. Your son has explicitly told you that he's busy with studies and needs space, and you should respect that. By not giving him the space he needs, you may be inadvertently creating more distance between the two of you. Additionally, your comment about the apartment needing a good clean, although possibly well-intentioned, came across as judgmental and critical. This might have made your son feel embarrassed, defensive, or annoyed, which could have been avoided if you had approached the situation with more sensitivity and respect. It's essential to remember that your son is now an adult, living independently, and needs to be treated as such. Giving him space and respecting his boundaries will help build trust and strengthen your relationship in the long run.
